summary: The note covers the final round of the 2023 AFLW home-and-away season, in which Gold Coast made finals for a second time and Sydney snatched eighth spot on the last day, ahead of St Kilda. It also reports Brisbane's win over Melbourne, Geelong's home-final advantage, North Melbourne's top-four lock, and emotional farewells for Erin Phillips and Richelle Cranston. The week-one finals fixture is listed at the top.
one_line: Gold Coast and Sydney reached the 2023 AFLW finals on the last round, while Erin Phillips and Richelle Cranston retired.
key_facts: Week one AFLW finals open Saturday November 11 with Adelaide v Brisbane Lions at Norwood Oval and Gold Coast v Sydney at Heritage Bank Stadium; Sunday November 12 has Geelong v Essendon at GMHBA Stadium and Melbourne v North Melbourne at Ikon Park.

Sydney beat Fremantle 5.10 (40) to 2.6 (18) at Fremantle Oval to take eighth spot and its first AFLW finals appearance, only 0.4 of a percentage point ahead of St Kilda; the Swans had been winless in their first season.
St Kilda beat Carlton 7.4 (46) to 3.8 (26) earlier that day but missed out on what would have been a maiden finals appearance.
Sydney's Laura Gardiner, a 20-year-old off-season recruit from Geelong, had a game-high 33 disposals and 18 contested possessions with ruck Ally Morphett out for the season with a wrist injury.
Brisbane Lions beat Melbourne 8.5 (53) to 4.4 (28) at Brighton Homes Arena, finishing fourth with a double chance, and Adelaide took the minor premiership from Melbourne.
Brisbane captain Bre Koenen held Melbourne's Kate Hore to one goal and had a game-high 12 intercept possessions; it was coach Craig Starcevich's 75th game.
Geelong beat Hawthorn 9.6 (60) to 3.2 (20), finished sixth with a percentage of 141.2, and secured home-ground advantage for the first elimination final; Chloe Scheer kicked three goals.
Erin Phillips played her last AFLW game, a 58-point win for Port Adelaide over Greater Western Sydney, 13.10 (88) to 4.6 (30), after eight seasons, 67 games and three premierships.
Western Bulldogs forward Richelle Cranston, an inaugural AFLW player, retired due to stage five chronic kidney disease and will start dialysis in January.
North Melbourne beat the Western Bulldogs 7.13 (55) to 1.3 (9) to lock in third spot and the double chance; Ash Riddell had 36 touches and seven clearances.
Britney Gutknecht's goal early in the final term saved the Bulldogs from the lowest score in AFLW history; they won one game and used 32 players, the most of any club.

Gold Coast beat Essendon 6.3 (39) to 3.7 (25) at Great Barrier Reef Arena to finish fifth, their second finals berth after the cancelled 2020 season; Lucy Single had 25 disposals and six clearances while Charlie Rowbottom was out injured.
